name: 1 Peter
author: The letter names Simon Peter as its writer. He was a fisherman from Galilee, in northern Israel, who became one of Jesus' twelve closest disciples and later a leading figure in the early church. Many scholars instead think a follower of Peter wrote it in his name after his death, drawing on his teaching. The letter also mentions Silvanus, who may have helped write or carry it.
audience: The letter is addressed to Christians scattered across five Roman provinces in what is now northern and western Turkey. Many seem to have been non-Jews who had left their old religious and social customs behind. Because of this, neighbours treated them with suspicion, slander and hostility, and they lived like outsiders in their own towns.
era: The Roman Empire ruled the whole Mediterranean world, and everyday life was bound up with honouring the emperor and the local gods. Christians who refused to take part could be seen as odd, disloyal or even dangerous. Tradition dates the letter to the early 60s AD, shortly before Peter was put to death in Rome under the emperor Nero; many scholars prefer a date between about AD 70 and 90.

notes.2:11: Christians were often accused of being troublemakers, and this section addresses life under the emperor and the provincial governors who kept order for Rome.
notes.2:18: Roman households expected slaves and wives to follow the master's religion; this section addresses household slaves and wives married to husbands who were not believers.
notes.4:12: The label "Christian" was still new, often used by outsiders as an insult; scholars debate whether this suffering was local hostility or official persecution.
notes.5:1: Elders were the older, trusted leaders who looked after each local congregation; the writer speaks to them as a fellow elder.
notes.5:12: Silvanus is probably the Silas who travelled with Paul, Mark is likely the gospel writer, and "Babylon" is widely understood as a code name for Rome.

flags.problem: 'Five Roman provinces' is doubtful. The letter names five regions (Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, Bithynia), but Pontus and Bithynia were then governed together as one province. 'Northern and western Turkey' is also too narrow, since Galatia and Cappadocia lie in central and eastern Turkey.
flags.suggestion: Say 'scattered across five regions of what is now Turkey' or 'across the Roman provinces of Asia Minor, in what is now Turkey'.

flags.problem: The section speaks to wives in general and allows that some had unbelieving husbands. It does not address only wives married to unbelievers. It also goes on to address husbands, so the summary is inaccurate.
flags.suggestion: Rephrase as 'this section addresses household slaves, wives (some married to husbands who were not believers) and husbands.'

flags.problem: 'Mark is likely the gospel writer' joins two separate traditions into one. The first is that this Mark is the John Mark known from Acts, which is widely accepted. The second is that John Mark wrote the Gospel of Mark, which is traditional but debated because the gospel itself names no author. As written, the note reads as more certain than the evidence allows.
flags.suggestion: Say 'Mark is probably the John Mark known from Paul's travels, whom early tradition links with the Gospel of Mark.'
